translation:
  text: '“How, sir,” I said, “did they become worse after coming to know God?”[a] “A person who does not
    know God and does evil,” he said, “receives some punishment for that evil. But someone who has come
    to know God ought no longer to do evil, but to do good.”


    2. “So if someone who loves to do good[b] does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil
    than someone who does not know God? That is why those who do evil without knowing God have been condemned
    to death. But those who have known God and seen his mighty works, yet do evil, will be punished doubly
    and die forever. In this way God’s church will be purified.”


    3. “Just as you saw the stones removed[c] from the tower and handed over to the evil spirits, those
    people too will be thrown out. There will be one body of those who have been purified, just as the
    tower appeared to be made of a single stone after its purification. So it will be with God’s church
    after it has been purified and the evil people, hypocrites, blasphemers, those of divided allegiance,
    and those who practice all kinds of evil have been cast out.”


    4. “After these people have been cast out, God’s church will be one body, with one outlook, one mind,
    one faith and one love. Then the Son of God will rejoice and be glad among them, having received his
    people back in purity.” “Everything is great and glorious, sir,” I said.


    5. “One more thing, sir,” I said.[d] “Explain to me the meaning and actions of each mountain, so that
    every person who trusts in the Lord may hear and glorify his great, wonderful and glorious name.”
    “Listen,” he said, “to the differences among the mountains and the twelve nations.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The first “God” is attested as an overlined abbreviation in the Codex Sinaiticus Project’s
      primary transcription (v1.05,Q95F8v col3 lines12–14), with no supply or correction mark on the noun.
      This corroborates the older printed God conjecture. Athos is reported as “Christ,” Latin Vulgata
      as “the Lord,” and Ethiopic is uncertain. Alternatives: “How, sir, did they become worse after coming
      to know Christ?” or “after coming to know the Lord?” The Sinaiticus following verb is corrected
      by hand ca to the come-to-know form; the original verb differs. No fresh image collation is claimed.
      “Sir” addresses the shepherd.'
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Who loves to do good” selects the Sinaiticus primary transcription,Q95F8v col3 lines23–25.
      Its finalι/ν in the good-doing infinitive are dotted as uncertain; neither verb is supplied. The
      older printed conjecture, compared with the Latin traditions and Ethiopic, is “who ought to do good”;
      reported Athos has approximately “who loves greatly.” Alternative: “So if someone who ought to do
      good does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil than someone who does not know God?”
      The bounded source selection changes only this verb phrase; the other Sinaiticus differences are
      not silently adopted.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Removed” translates the printed restoration of damaged Athos, including conjecturally supplied
      initial letters. The following “those people too will be thrown out” follows Harmer’s conjecture
      compared with Latin Palatina; the apparatus reports Athos/Ethiopic approximately “from there, having
      been thrown out.” Neither printed completion is certified as fully surviving Greek.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “I said” is bracketed in the printed source. It identifies the continuing dialogue rather than
      adding a new speaker.

  text: '“How, sir,” I said, “did they become worse after coming to know God?”[a] “A person who does not
    know God and does evil,” he said, “receives some punishment for that evil. But someone who has come
    to know God ought no longer to do evil, but to do good.”


    2. “So if someone who loves to do good[b] does evil, does that person not seem to do greater evil
    than someone who does not know God? That is why those who do evil without knowing God have been condemned
    to death. But those who have known God and seen his mighty works, yet do evil, will be punished doubly
    and die forever. In this way God’s church will be purified.”


    3. “Just as you saw the stones removed[c] from the tower and handed over to the evil spirits, those
    people too will be thrown out. There will be one body of those who have been purified, just as the
    tower appeared to be made of a single stone after its purification. So it will be with God’s church
    after it has been purified and the evil people, hypocrites, blasphemers, those of divided allegiance,
    and those who practice all kinds of evil have been cast out.”


    4. “After these people have been cast out, God’s church will be one body, with one outlook, one mind,
    one faith and one love. Then the Son of God will rejoice and be glad among them, having received his
    people back in purity.” “Everything is great and glorious, sir,” I said.


    5. “One more thing, sir,” I said.[d] “Explain to me the meaning and actions of each mountain, so that
    every person who trusts in the Lord may hear and glorify his great, wonderful and glorious name.”
    “Listen,” he said, “to the differences among the mountains and the twelve nations.”'
